text: The early church "continued steadfastly" in four things: the apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers.
explanation:
Three thousand had just been saved at Pentecost, and they held fast to four pillars. They taught Christ and His finished work, shared life together, came back to the Lord's Table again and again, and prayed. The result: "Many wonders and signs were done through the apostles… And the Lord added to the church daily those who were being saved."

Most churches today emphasise one or two of these and neglect the others. Your personal life needs all four as well. Going through a trial? Don't face it alone. Hear the Word, reach out to brothers and sisters, take communion, and pray.

text: Jesus "increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour." The early church had "favour with all the people." Luke ends both chapter 2s with favour and growth.
explanation:
Luke wrote two accounts for Theophilus. His Gospel tells of the birth of Christ "when the fullness of the time had come"; Acts tells of the birth of the church "when the Day of Pentecost had fully come." Each covers about thirty years. In both, the Holy Spirit is the agent of birth: overshadowing Mary and filling the disciples.

And each second chapter closes in parallel: Jesus growing in stature and favour, and the church growing as the Lord added daily, "having favour with all the people." What Jesus did in His earthly body, He now does through His body, the church. As you're part of it, His favour and growth are your story too.

text: "Where two or three are gathered together in My name": not "meet," but are gathered, by the Holy Spirit.
explanation:
Two friends chatting at a café aren't automatically a church. The verb is passive: they are gathered. Someone else does the gathering, and that's the Holy Spirit. When He brings believers together, even the smallest plurality of two, Jesus promises, "There I am in the midst of them."

And that gathered church is on the offensive. "The gates of Hades shall not prevail against it." Gates don't attack; they defend. The church is advancing, and hell's gates are the ones under pressure. Don't let the visible failures of some discourage you. His church is growing worldwide, and it will outlast every human institution.

text: You don't have to preach at work. Just by being there, you're the salt that keeps things from going bad.
explanation:
In Jesus' day salt was the refrigerator; it kept food from corrupting. You carry the Holy Spirit into your office, your classroom and your home, and there's a sanctifying influence simply because you're there. Things could be far worse if you weren't.

Scripture speaks of a restrainer holding back lawlessness until he is taken out of the way. Imagine the world when the church is gone. So don't wish you could hide in an all-Christian environment. If all the salt stays in the shaker, what good is it? Get out there; you're needed exactly where you are.

text: A lamp isn't lit to go under a bushel or a bed. When God lights you up, He sets you on the lampstand.
explanation:
The bushel was a measuring basket for grain, the tool of commerce. The bed can picture laziness or sexual sin. Either can smother the light God has given you. When David took Bathsheba and had her husband killed, the man's name was Uriah, "the Lord is my light." It was as if David put out God's light in his own life.

Money-making is part of life, but beware of being obsessed with it, especially schemes that promise quick riches. Jesus said a lamp belongs "on a lampstand," and the lampstands in Revelation are the churches. That's where your light shines brightest, blessing both your church and your household, and drawing in those who are searching.

text: "You earn wages to put into a bag with holes… because of My house that is in ruins."
explanation:
The exiles came home from Babylon and set about panelling their own houses while God's house lay in ruins. Through Haggai, God described what happened: "You eat, but do not have enough; you drink, but you are not filled… and he who earns wages, earns wages to put into a bag with holes." No matter how much came in, it was never enough.

God's answer is to put first what He puts first. "Honour the Lord with your possessions, and with the firstfruits of all your increase; so your barns will be filled with plenty." Prioritise His house, His people and His purposes, and He'll take care of your bag.

text: Mary anointed Jesus at the right time. The other women came on the third day with spices, and it was too late.
explanation:
Mary of Bethany poured costly oil on Jesus days before the cross, and He said, "She has kept this for the day of My burial." On resurrection morning, other devoted women came to the tomb to anoint His body, but He had already risen.

Mary didn't have special inside information. She had simply spent her time at His feet, occupied with Him. You don't have to anxiously work out whether you're in the right place at the right time. Keep your heart on Jesus, and you'll find yourself doing the right thing at the right moment.
